summary: Sends DMX data to DMX, Art-Net, sACN, KiNET, or FTDI devices by merging DMX Fixture POP inputs into output universes.

key_params.name: active
key_params.note: Actively send data to the selected DMX device/interface

key_params.name: interface
key_params.note: Generic Serial, Enttec USB Pro, Art-Net, sACN, or KiNET output interface

key_params.name: fixture
key_params.note: Sequential DMX Fixture POP input blocks

key_params.name: fixture0active
key_params.note: Merge and send this fixture block

key_params.name: fixture0pop
key_params.note: Referenced DMX Fixture POPs when no corresponding input is wired

key_params.name: serialport
key_params.note: Serial COM port for Generic Serial interface

key_params.name: netaddress
key_params.note: Target device IP address or broadcast address

key_params.name: localaddress
key_params.note: Local network adapter/address to send from

key_params.name: localport
key_params.note: Custom local source port or OS-assigned default

key_params.name: sendartsync
key_params.note: Send ArtSync packets after ArtDmx packets

key_params.name: routingtable
key_params.note: Optional table of netaddress, source, cid, priority, and KiNET port per universe

key_concepts: DMX Out POP sends merged DMX universes from DMX Fixture POP inputs to serial, USB, Art-Net, sACN, KiNET, or FTDI output paths.
Every wired or referenced input is expected to be a DMX Fixture POP; fixture sequence blocks can be active/inactive and can reference fixture POPs by OP pattern.
Multiple fixture sources can be merged into one output, but channel conflicts in the same universe produce warnings and should be debugged with DMX Map DAT.
Network output separates target addressing from universe layout: netaddress, local adapter, ports, priority, ArtSync, KiNET, and routing table rows control transmission behavior.
Broadcast is supported, but the docs recommend unicast for large universe counts to avoid overwhelming the network.
common_gotchas: Every input should be a DMX Fixture POP, either wired or referenced by parameter.
Multiple fixture inputs writing the same channel in the same universe can conflict and produce warnings.
Unicast can be preferable to broadcast for large numbers of universes.
